title: Repo Audit, November 2026
eyebrow: Full audit of every code file in AjsClaudeCodeTools · nothing changed yet

short.lead: I read every code file in the repo, with two forked helpers taking the two biggest parts of the plugin, and I re-ran every probe they used. All four test suites pass, but the guard that is meant to stop risky commands has six real holes. A commit with a hidden program inside it is approved with no prompt. Four delete forms and four forms that throw away edits get no decision at all. Any merged pull request unlocks closing any issue. Cloud sessions can't commit to the branch they are told to push. Reading a script counts as running it. There are 20 findings in all, plus about 380 lines that can go.
short.hint: Tap a card to see the evidence behind it.
items: Every code file, with each helper's result re-run

The main session read tools/, the standalone scripts, both smaller plugins, CI and the guard. One helper read design_loop.py and delegation.py, and the other read core.py, docs.py, writing.py, hook.py and the rest of safe_git.py. Each finding was proved by feeding the real hook a command and reading its decision, except four marked 'by reading' in the report. The test files under checks/ were searched, not read in full.
Six holes in the guard and the issue lock

1: a commit carrying $(...), backticks or -c core.hooksPath is approved, which also skips Claude Code's own prompt. 2: any merged pull request unlocks closing any QA-passed issue. 3: /bin/rm -rf, find -delete, unlink and ': > file' get no decision. 4: git checkout HEAD -- FILE, git checkout HEAD FILE, git checkout -f and git switch -f get no decision. 5: agent/ branches count as not the agent's own, so cloud sessions can't commit where they must push. 6: cat, grep or git commit naming a .py file counts as running it.
Locks that fail open, and tools that report wrongly

The stage file that locks code edits is rewritten in place, so a hook reading it mid-write turns the lock off. A cp from the shell can overwrite it, and three helpers launched together all pass the two-helper cap. The installer can empty settings.json if a write fails, and its check for changed files always reports a difference. Autosave pushes untracked files, a stray token file included. The version check 'updates' a newer copy down to an older one.

tools/check_verify_inventory.py (304 lines) checks a finished test-suite split, and nothing runs it. There are 55 blank lines left over in safe_git.py, a dead line in clarity.py, a never-filled list in hook.py, two checkpoint rows that can't fire, and a second Markdown fence parser beside a correct one.
Choose the scope of the first fix, and whether the unused inventory checker is deleted or added to CI. Approving starts the fix as a feature, with one issue per step and a test for each hole.
Send "Design approved: audit fixes" with your two picks, or tell me what to change.

changes: chg
1. Commits that run a program are approved unasked
safe_git.py:744-745 and _only_git_statements at :384-387.
Any statement starting with git is approved, $(...), backticks and -c core.hooksPath included.
Approved only when there is no $( or backtick outside the $(cat <<'EOF' message form and no core.hooksPath; otherwise Claude Code asks.
Proved: a commit with $(...), one with backticks and one with core.hooksPath each got allow.
chg
2. Any merge unlocks any issue close
design_loop.py:2123-2129.
A merge in other/repo#99 stamped and unlocked the close of own/repo#5.
Only a merge in the same repo that names the issue with Refs #N unlocks its close.
Proved: the close went from deny to allow after the unrelated merge.
chg
3 and 4. Delete and discard forms the guard misses
safe_git.py:133 and :143.
/bin/rm -rf, find -delete, unlink, ': > file', checkout HEAD -- FILE, checkout -f and switch -f all got no decision.
Each form is refused the way rm -rf and checkout -- already are, keeping the saved-work exemption.
Proved: each command was fed to the real guard.
chg
5. agent/ branches are the agent's own
core.py:2089 and safe_git.py:265-301.
Commit refused on agent/optimistic-planck-1h64c9, the branch this session must push to.
agent/ joins AjsAgent/, claude/ and ccr- as an owned prefix.
Proved: this session's own commit was refused.
chg
6. Reading a script no longer counts as running it
safe_git.py:464-478.
Any word that names an existing .py, .sh or similar file counts as running it, so a second sed of safe_git.py was refused.
Only the first word, or the first argument after python, sh, bash, node or pwsh, counts.
Proved: a second sed of safe_git.py was refused during this audit.
chg
7, 9 and 10. The stage lock and the helper cap hold
design_loop.py, delegation.py, safe_git.py and make_page.py writers.
State files are emptied and rewritten in place; an empty stage file turns the lock off; cp overwrites it; three helpers launched together all pass.
Writes go to a per-process temp file and os.replace; a shell command naming the stage file is refused unless read-only; agentcap adds a placeholder record.
Proved by runs, except the race where two writers overwrite each other's changes, which is by reading.
chg
8, 12, 13 and 16. Install and update tell the truth
tools/install.py, core.py:1327-1338, tools/_plugin_sync.py, tools/force_update.py.
settings.json is rewritten in place; 2.75.0 is 'updated' to 1.0.0; every install finds __pycache__ as a difference; a failed reinstall leaves no guard without saying so.
Atomic settings write, an older-than comparison, cache files skipped in the hash, and a clear message when the reinstall fails.
Proved by runs, except the settings write and the force-update failure, which are by reading.
chg
11, 14 and 15. Leaks and wrong answers
delegation.py:1252-1290, make_page.py:569-578, docs.py:208.
Autosave adds untracked files with git add -A; the node visual check looks for playwright in a different folder from the probe; two commit -a patterns disagree on whether -sam counts as commit -a.
git add -u plus files the helper wrote; node -e and a deleted temp file; one shared pattern.
Autosave is by reading, because a run would push to the real remote.
new
17. A test for every hole
One case each in checks/safe_git.py, checks/design_loop.py and checks/delegation.py.
No case covers any of the commands above, which is why every suite passes today.
Every suite passes with all six holes open.
Each fix lands with the test that would have caught it.
The holes can't come back unnoticed.

18 to 20. Lean cleanup
About 380 lines, no dependencies.

check_verify_inventory.py, 55 blank lines, dead code in clarity.py, hook.py and design_loop.py, a second fence parser, a failed self-heal counted twice in tools/install.py, and diff_parts.py dropping lines that start with -- or ++.
